purpose: P-T8 (pre-registered): does grouping the conformal calibration/evaluation split by borehole or by ~500 m site -- instead of by row -- change target-region coverage, interval width or Winkler score? The published figures used a random ROW split of the held-out region, so sibling layers of one borehole land on both sides of the split.
bar: marginal coverage gap at alpha=0.95 <= 0.01 under the grouped split, and mean interval width within +20% of the row split
verdict: CONFIRMED -- and an informative negative for the reviewer's concern
interpretation: Across all eight leave-region-out cells (216k-496k held-out rows, 15.7k-30.5k boreholes) the pre-registered bar is met with margin under BOTH grouped split units: the worst single-cell absolute coverage gap at alpha=0.95 is 0.00341 for the borehole split and 0.00527 for the site split, both inside the 0.01 bar, and every cell's mean interval width is within 1% of the row split's (bar: +20%). Sibling-layer dependence therefore does not inflate the reported conformal coverage at this calibration size: the marginal quantile of the conformity score is estimated from >100k residuals either way, so grouping changes its effective sample size but not its value. Two qualifications belong with that claim and are recorded in per_cell_worst_case_vs_row_split. First, the agreement is tightest for the BOREHOLE split; the ~500 m SITE split is looser -- worst single-cell coverage difference 0.0176 and width difference 4.97% (kansai, alpha=0.5) -- so the manuscript should quote the borehole split, which is also the unit the objection was about. Second, the caveat that survives is CONDITIONAL rather than marginal: coverage is uneven across geological regimes, markedly so at alpha=0.5, which is what the Mondrian binning addresses and what the SI reports per regime.
